posts.title: How I'd set a minimum price before matching the guy down the street
posts.text: Don't start from "what the guy down the street charges." Start from what the stop actually costs, then set a floor, then check the market. Build a fully loaded cost for each job: on-site labor (wage plus payroll burden), windshield time, mileage, materials, and a slice of weekly overhead (insurance, phone, software, unpaid admin, equipment). The minimum price at your target margin is: Minimum price = Fully loaded cost ÷ (1 − target margin) EXAMPLE only — not a recommended price and not a... posts.title: How do you handle price changes on a job once you're into it?
posts.text: Curious how other guys handle this. I'll quote a job based on what I can see, then get into a wall or under a floor and find rot, bad wiring, whatever — something there was no way to know about walking through it. Now I've got to have the "this is going to cost more" conversation, and even when I'm straight with people about why, some of them hear it as "the guy padded the price after he had me locked in." Had one a while back where the homeowner got a few other quotes after mine changed... How do you handle price changes on a job once you're into it?
